Domestic Violence, hereinafter referred to as KDRT, is any act against someone, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business determined by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare with emphasis on voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capabilities and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of acts of violence, abuse, KDRT, exploitation, abuse or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving region to the region of origin. 25. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in the community. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30.

Article 26

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability on the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1. physical harassment;
2. verbal harassment;
3. gestural harassment;
4. written or pictorial harassment; and
5. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. coercion into sexual intercourse;
c. coercion into unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse; and/or
d. coercion into sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes: a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill the needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or attend to children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 8

(1) Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

(2) Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.

(3) Protection of women's rights in employment rights inside or outside the country receives protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.

(4) Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.

(5) Protection of women's rights from trafficking in persons includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

Article 7

The implementation of women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in Article 3 letter d includes:

a. improvement of knowledge and awareness in the field of law through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and consultation services as well as free legal aid.

Article 31

(1) The Village Government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, has the obligation and responsibility to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence; c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence in accordance with village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the village medium-term development plan.

Article 33

(1) Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and report if violence occurs and protect victims.

(2) In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) are absent or their whereabouts are unknown or for some reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 64

(1) Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, resulting in the occurrence of violence, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-district Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection tasks, if they violate the principles of protection, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 64

(1) Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, resulting in the occurrence of violence, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-district Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection tasks, if they violate the principles of protection, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 8

(1) Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

(2) Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.

(3) Protection of women's rights in employment rights inside or outside the country receives protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.

(4) Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.

(5) Protection of women's rights from trafficking in persons includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

Article 13

(1) Protection of children in the civil and freedom field assists children so that children can:

a. participate in all fields;
b. freely express opinions and think in accordance with conscience and religion in accordance with the norms applicable in the region; c. freely receive oral or written information in accordance with the age stages and development of the child;
d. freely associate and assemble in accordance with noble norms and ethics; e. freely rest, play, recreate, and create arts and culture without neglecting obligations as a child; and
f. obtain play facilities that meet health and safety requirements.
(2) Efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are developed and adjusted to the age, level of ability of the child, and their environment so as not to hinder and disturb the development of the child.

Article 26

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability on the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1. physical harassment;
2. verbal harassment;
3. gestural harassment;
4. written or pictorial harassment; and
5. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. coercion into sexual intercourse;
c. coercion into unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse; and/or
d. coercion into sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes: a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill the needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or attend to children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 26

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability on the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1. physical harassment;
2. verbal harassment;
3. gestural harassment;
4. written or pictorial harassment; and
5. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. coercion into sexual intercourse;
c. coercion into unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse; and/or
d. coercion into sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes: a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill the needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or attend to children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that fall under the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution that serves as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that fall under the authority of the Regency region. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to enhance physical, mental, spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is someone who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 9. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 12. Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence, hereinafter referred to as KDRT, is any act against someone, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business determined by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare with emphasis on voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capabilities and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of acts of violence, abuse, KDRT, exploitation, abuse or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving region to the region of origin. 25. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in the community. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30.

Article 64

(1) Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, resulting in the occurrence of violence, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-district Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection tasks, if they violate the principles of protection, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 9

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to provide protection to women in order to realize and enjoy a decent standard of living.

(2) Provisions regarding Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VIII

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 26

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability on the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1. physical harassment;
2. verbal harassment;
3. gestural harassment;
4. written or pictorial harassment; and
5. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. coercion into sexual intercourse;
c. coercion into unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse; and/or
d. coercion into sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes: a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill the needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or attend to children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in the community. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30.

Article 46

UPTD PPPA as referred to in Article 45 letter a is the technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children experiencing problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

CHAPTER VIII

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 9

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to provide protection to women in order to realize and enjoy a decent standard of living.

(2) Provisions regarding Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 34

The Regional Government implements activities for the administration of women's protection and child protection, which include:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. social rehabilitation.

Article 26

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability on the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1. physical harassment;
2. verbal harassment;
3. gestural harassment;
4. written or pictorial harassment; and
5. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. coercion into sexual intercourse;
c. coercion into unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse; and/or
d. coercion into sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes: a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill the needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or attend to children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 32. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, Integrated Crisis Centers (PKT), Integrated Service Centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women crisis centers, training centers, Science and Technology Information Centers (PIPTEK), shelters, transit houses, or other forms. 33. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Sub-district level. 34. Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Village level. 35. Article 32

(1) The Community as referred to in Article 29 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 64

(1) Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, resulting in the occurrence of violence, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-district Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection tasks, if they violate the principles of protection, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Part Seven

Child Protection in the Field of Special Protection

Article 31

(1) The Village Government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, has the obligation and responsibility to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence; c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence in accordance with village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the village medium-term development plan.

The Regional Government implements activities for the administration of women's protection and child protection, which include:

a. prevention;
b. services; and

(5) Protection of women's rights from trafficking in persons includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

Article 26

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability on the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1. physical harassment;
2. verbal harassment;
3. gestural harassment;
4. written or pictorial harassment; and
5. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. coercion into sexual intercourse;
c. coercion into unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse; and/or
d. coercion into sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes: a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill the needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or attend to children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 9

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to provide protection to women in order to realize and enjoy a decent standard of living.

(2) Provisions regarding Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in the community. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly. 29. DECIDES :

To Stipulate : REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING WOMEN EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION.

CHAPTER III

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 34

The Regional Government implements activities for the administration of women's protection and child protection, which include:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. social rehabilitation.

Article 31

(1) The Village Government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, has the obligation and responsibility to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence; c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence in accordance with village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the village medium-term development plan.

Part Seven

Child Protection in the Field of Special Protection

Article 33

(1) Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and report if violence occurs and protect victims.

(2) In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) are absent or their whereabouts are unknown or for some reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 8

(1) Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

(2) Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.

(3) Protection of women's rights in employment rights inside or outside the country receives protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.

(4) Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.

(5) Protection of women's rights from trafficking in persons includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

Article 46

UPTD PPPA as referred to in Article 45 letter a is the technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children experiencing problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.

Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA, is a technical implementing body to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children who experience problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 32. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, Integrated Crisis Centers (PKT), Integrated Service Centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women crisis centers, training centers, Science and Technology Information Centers (PIPTEK), shelters, transit houses, or other forms. 33. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Sub-district level. 34. Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Village level. 35. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 36. Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is a coordinating institution at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency. 37. Regional Action Plan for the Development of a Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.

CHAPTER VIII

PROVISION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 34

The Regional Government implements activities for the administration of women's protection and child protection, which include:

a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. social rehabilitation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that fall under the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution that serves as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that fall under the authority of the Regency region. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to enhance physical, mental, spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is someone who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 9. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 12. Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence, hereinafter referred to as KDRT, is any act against someone, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business determined by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare with emphasis on voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capabilities and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of acts of violence, abuse, KDRT, exploitation, abuse or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving region to the region of origin. 25. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in the community. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30.

Article 32

(1) The Community as referred to in Article 29 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 31

(1) The Village Government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, has the obligation and responsibility to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence; c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence in accordance with village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the village medium-term development plan.

Article 26

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability on the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1. physical harassment;
2. verbal harassment;
3. gestural harassment;
4. written or pictorial harassment; and
5. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. coercion into sexual intercourse;
c. coercion into unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse; and/or
d. coercion into sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes: a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill the needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or attend to children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 64

(1) Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, resulting in the occurrence of violence, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) The management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-district Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection tasks, if they violate the principles of protection, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 21

(1) Supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse as referred to in Article 17 letter d and involved in their production and distribution, is the obligation and responsibility of the Regional Government and the community.

(2) The implementation of protection for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in the form of:

a. Prevention Services, including:
1. Making policies for the protection of children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; 2. Making special protection policies for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; and
3. Providing socialization and raising awareness of parents and/or the community and children regarding the adverse effects of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse.
b. Risk Reduction Services, which include:
1. Conducting early identification, complaint services and assessment of children and families at risk;
2. Providing services for children and families who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse including:
a. guidance and counseling on parenting patterns and behavioral change;
b. legal consultation; and
c. psychosocial services.
c. Case Handling Services, including:
1. Making immediate rescue efforts for victims who are in dangerous conditions for their safety;
2. Providing referrals according to the needs of victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; 3. Conducting counseling and support from the family; 4. Treating child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse in a humane manner in accordance with the dignity and rights of children; and
5. Providing rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

Article 8

(1) Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

(2) Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.

(3) Protection of women's rights in employment rights inside or outside the country receives protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.

(4) Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that fall under the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution that serves as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element to the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that fall under the authority of the Regency region. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to enhance physical, mental, spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is someone who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 9. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 12. Violence against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and abuse that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence, hereinafter referred to as KDRT, is any act against someone, especially women, that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the household sphere. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct ascending or descending line up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business determined by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare with emphasis on voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capabilities and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of acts of violence, abuse, KDRT, exploitation, abuse or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving region to the region of origin. 25. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disruption to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to perform their role again properly both in the family and in the community. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to perform social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30.

Article 26

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability on the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1. physical harassment;
2. verbal harassment;
3. gestural harassment;
4. written or pictorial harassment; and
5. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. coercion into sexual intercourse;
c. coercion into unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse; and/or
d. coercion into sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes: a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill the needs of children, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or attend to children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes: a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent that include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or sexual abuse activities.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without the use of means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 32

(1) The Community as referred to in Article 29 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 59

(1) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in Article 58 paragraph (3) letter b is prepared for a period of 5 (five) years or as needed which is integrated with the regional medium-term development plan, and the work plan of regional apparatus.

(2) The Regional Action Plan has an annual program focus that refers to the stages of achieving Child-Friendly Regency indicators.

(3) The Child-Friendly Regency Regional Action Plan must be based on field problems and their comprehensive resolution. (4) The Regional Action Plan is socialized to all Regional Apparatus, child stakeholders, families, and communities.

(5) Further provisions regarding the Child-Friendly Regency Regional Action Plan are stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA, is a technical implementing body to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children who experience problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 32. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Regional Government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, Integrated Crisis Centers (PKT), Integrated Service Centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women crisis centers, training centers, Science and Technology Information Centers (PIPTEK), shelters, transit houses, or other forms. 33. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Sub-district level. 34. Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children is a functional Work Unit that organizes protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women in an integrated manner at the Village level. 35. Child-Friendly Regency is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 36. Child-Friendly Regency Task Force is a coordinating institution at the regency level that coordinates policy efforts, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency. 37. Regional Action Plan for the Development of a Child-Friendly Regency is a document containing policies, programs and activities to realize a child-friendly regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 31

(1) The Village Government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, has the obligation and responsibility to:

a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence; c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence in accordance with village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the village medium-term development plan.

CHAPTER XIV

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 21

(1) Supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse as referred to in Article 17 letter d and involved in their production and distribution, is the obligation and responsibility of the Regional Government and the community.

(2) The implementation of protection for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in the form of:

a. Prevention Services, including:
1. Making policies for the protection of children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; 2. Making special protection policies for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; and
3. Providing socialization and raising awareness of parents and/or the community and children regarding the adverse effects of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse.
b. Risk Reduction Services, which include:
1. Conducting early identification, complaint services and assessment of children and families at risk;
2. Providing services for children and families who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse including:
a. guidance and counseling on parenting patterns and behavioral change;
b. legal consultation; and
c. psychosocial services.
c. Case Handling Services, including:
1. Making immediate rescue efforts for victims who are in dangerous conditions for their safety;
2. Providing referrals according to the needs of victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; 3. Conducting counseling and support from the family; 4. Treating child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse in a humane manner in accordance with the dignity and rights of children; and
5. Providing rehabilitation and social reintegration services.
